entry.englishMeaning: to investigate something to understand or resolve it
entry.coreIdea: Shine a torch inside the problem.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract phrasal verb for investigating a matter; here, find out what is wrong with the heating.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral: it promises investigation, not necessarily immediate repair or a successful outcome.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Matter-of-fact here: the sentence reports the landlord's promise to investigate.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common everyday and workplace English. “Investigate” is more formal.

when_to_use: Promise to investigate a heating complaint and give a follow-up time. A model in this sense: The school will look into the missing lunch payments.
when_not_to_use: Do not use look into to claim a problem has already been solved; it describes investigation.

advanced_nuance: Look into leaves the outcome of an investigation open. Adding a realistic update time makes the promise more useful without guaranteeing a repair.
Look into is inseparable in this sense: look into it, not look it into.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Shine a torch inside the problem.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: The school will look into the missing lunch payments.
memory_practice.production_task: Promise to investigate a heating complaint and give a follow-up time. Respond in one or two natural sentences using the expression, then compare with the pattern after answering.
memory_practice.recall_question: Recall the expression for this meaning without looking: to investigate something to understand or resolve it. Explain its function in one sentence.
memory_practice.recognition_task: A landlord promises to look into a heating problem. Does this establish that the heating has been repaired? Explain what the promise actually covers.

examples.scenario: The landlord promised to look into the heating problem.
examples.another_setting: The school will look into the missing lunch payments.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: The school will look into the missing lunch payments.
B: When should I expect an update?
A: We’ll contact you by Friday, even if the investigation is still open.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: The landlord promised to look into the heating problem.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: to investigate something to understand or resolve it
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The landlord has promised to investigate what is wrong with the heating. This does not tell us that the cause has been found or the problem repaired.

mistakes_differences.correction: We will look into the issue.
mistakes_differences.common_mistake: We will look the issue into.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Look into means investigate. Sort out means resolve or organize the matter; looking into a problem may be the first step toward sorting it out.

semanticReview.finding: Valid investigation examples and grammar retained; investigation distinguished from resolution, conversation completed.

entry.englishMeaning: to become involved in a way that obstructs or disrupts
entry.coreIdea: Get involved in a way that others find disruptive.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract verb for unwanted involvement that disrupts or obstructs; here, involvement by in-laws that someone wants stopped.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Negative: it describes the involvement as unwelcome rather than simply helpful participation.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Problem-focused here: the example is listed among difficult conversations people may need to have.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common in personal and professional discussions, but it attributes an unwelcome effect. Describe the action when the judgement could be disputed.

when_to_use: Describe unwanted involvement in another person’s decisions or affairs.
when_not_to_use: Do not call requested help interference merely because another person participates.
In a sensitive discussion, identify the unwanted action rather than relying only on the accusation You interfere.

advanced_nuance: Interfere can sound accusatory because it judges the involvement negatively. I don’t want to interfere can soften an offer of advice, but the advice may still be unwelcome.
Interfere in focuses on entering someone’s affairs; interfere with can focus on disrupting their work or plans. In both patterns here, another person’s involvement is the issue.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Picture someone taking over a decision that belongs to another person.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: Please do not interfere in our decision.
memory_practice.recall_question: What judgement does interfere add to simply become involved?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A team asks an adviser for suggestions, and the adviser supplies them without taking over. Is interfere necessarily a fair description? Explain what unwanted involvement would add.
memory_practice.production_task: Write a calm request to a fictional colleague who keeps changing your team’s plans without consultation. Use interfere and name the action you want changed.

examples.example_1: Please do not interfere in our decision about where to live.
examples.example_2: The supervisor promised not to interfere with the team’s plans unless they asked for help.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: I’ve told your team to change the schedule.
B: Please don’t interfere in that decision; we are still discussing it together.
A: All right. I’ll share my concern with you first next time.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Other  topics  that  could  easily  lead  to  disaster  include  •  Ending  a  relationship  •  Talking  to  a  coworker  who  behaves  offen sively  or  makes  sugges­ tive  comments  •  Asking  a  friend  to  repay  a  loan  •  Giving  the  boss  fee dback  about  her  behavior  •  Approaching  a  boss  who  is  breaking  his  own  safety  or  quality  policies  •  Critiquing  a  colleague's  work  •  Asking  a  roommate  to  move  out  •  Resolving  custody  or  visitation  issues  with  an  ex-spouse  •  Dealing  with  a  rebellious  teen  •  Ta lking  to  a  team  member  who  isn't  keeping  commitments  •  Discussi ng  problems  with  sexual  intimacy  •  Confronting  a  loved  one  about  a  subs tance  abuse  problem  •  Talking to  a  colleague  who  is  hoarding  inf onnation  or  resources  •  Giving  an  unf avorab le  performance review  •  Asking  in-laws  to  quit  interfering  •  Talking  to  a  coworker  about  a  personal  hygiene  problem  OUR  AUDACIOUS  CLAI M  Let's  say  that  either  you  avoid  tough  issues  or  when  you  do  bring  them  up,   you're  on  your  worst  behavior.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: to become involved in a way that obstructs or disrupts
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The list includes asking in-laws to stop unwanted involvement. It does not describe the particular actions they took; interfering expresses the affected person’s negative judgement of that involvement.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: Please do not interfere our decision.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say Please do not interfere in our decision. Use a preposition before the matter someone becomes involved in.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Help presents involvement as useful. Interfere presents it as unwanted or disruptive; the people involved may disagree about that judgement.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: interfere in + someone’s affairs/decision; interfere with + someone’s work/plans

semanticReview.finding: Unwanted personal involvement sense preserved; preposition patterns and judgement distinguished from requested help.

entry.englishMeaning: the act or result of carefully noticing what happens
entry.coreIdea: What careful attention allows you to notice.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract noun for what someone notices through attentive watching; here, findings compared after observing conversations.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral: an observation is information to examine, not automatically a proven explanation.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Analytical and methodical here: comparing observations is followed by testing hypotheses and refining models.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Neutral to formal; common in research and reflective discussion. Distinguish observed behaviour from interpretations of its cause.

when_to_use: Report a detail noticed through attentive watching or listening, or describe the process of gathering such details.
when_not_to_use: Do not present an untested explanation of someone’s motive as if it were a direct observation.

advanced_nuance: Observation can be uncountable for the process, as in careful observation, or countable for a particular noticed detail, as in three observations.
An observation can still be mistaken or incomplete. Comparing observations helps identify differences in what people noticed; it does not automatically settle the explanation.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Picture two notebook columns: noticed details and possible explanations.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: We compared our observations after the discussion.
memory_practice.recall_question: How does an observation differ from a guess about a person’s motive?
memory_practice.recognition_task: Which is closer to a direct observation? A: She looked at the clock twice. B: She wanted us to leave. Explain what can be noticed and what has been inferred.
memory_practice.production_task: Write two sentences about a fictional meeting: one observation of visible or audible behaviour and one clearly labelled possible explanation.

examples.example_1: My observation was that three people spoke before anyone asked the new member a question.
examples.example_2: The students compared their observations of the birds feeding outside the classroom.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: What did you notice during the discussion?
B: My main observation was that she paused after every question.
A: Let’s record the pauses separately from our guesses about why they happened.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Afterward  we  compared  our  observations,  tested  our  hy potheses,  and  honed  our  models  until  we found  the  skills  that  consistently  explain  the  success  of  brilliant  communi cators .
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: the act or result of carefully noticing what happens
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The researchers compared what they had noticed, then tested possible explanations. Their observations are the noticed details, not automatically proof of why the conversations succeeded.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: An interpretation presented as a fact: My observation is that he stayed silent because he disliked us.
mistakes_differences.correction: Separate the claim: My observation is that he stayed silent. I do not yet know why.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: An observation describes what was noticed. An interpretation proposes what it means or why it happened; that explanation may need further evidence.

semanticReview.finding: Noticed evidence distinguished from causal interpretation; countable and uncountable uses explained.

entry.englishMeaning: a condition that must be met before participation or progress is possible
entry.coreIdea: A requirement that must be met before a process starts.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract condition-of-access metaphor: mutual purpose is presented as something required before dialogue can proceed.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Neutral as a requirement, while the passage treats mutual purpose as beneficial.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Definite and explanatory here: “is” presents the condition as an essential part of the method.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Formal explanatory wording. “A requirement for dialogue” is clearer in everyday language; it is not a physical entrance rule here.

when_to_use: State a required starting condition for participation in a process or discussion.
when_not_to_use: Do not call a desirable later result an entry condition if it is not required before the process begins.

advanced_nuance: Entry condition is formal process language. Requirement for starting is often clearer in ordinary conversation.
Meeting an entry condition allows a process to begin; it does not guarantee that the process will succeed.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Picture a required check completed before a discussion begins.
memory_practice.memory_sentence: A shared purpose is an entry condition for this dialogue method.
memory_practice.recall_question: When must an entry condition be met: before starting or only after finishing?
memory_practice.recognition_task: A group must agree on confidentiality before its discussion starts. Is that an entry condition or a final outcome? Explain the order.
memory_practice.production_task: Write a short note for a fictional group discussion naming one entry condition and explaining why the group needs it before beginning.

examples.example_1: Agreement on the topic is an entry condition for this structured discussion.
examples.example_2: For our joint planning exercise, sharing the relevant information is an entry condition, not an optional final step.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Can we start the joint planning session now?
B: We agreed that sharing the figures was an entry condition, and one team has not done that yet.
A: I’ll ask them to send the figures before we begin.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: Consequ ent ly,  Mutual  Purpo se  is  the  entry  condition  of  dialogue.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: a condition that must be met before participation or progress is possible
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The author treats a shared purpose as a requirement for starting constructive dialogue. This is a claim about the author’s method, not a rule for entering a physical place.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: Shared purpose is entry condition for this discussion.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say Shared purpose is an entry condition for this discussion. A singular countable phrase needs a determiner here.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: An entry condition must be met before participation or progress can begin. A desired outcome is something the process aims to produce afterward.

patterns_collocations.main_pattern: an entry condition for + process; meet/satisfy + an entry condition

semanticReview.finding: Starting requirement distinguished from desired outcome; source claim attributed to the dialogue method.

entry.englishMeaning: gained only after considerable effort or work
entry.coreIdea: Obtained through a lot of effort.

meaning_usage_profile.meaning_type: Abstract adjective emphasizing that something was obtained through substantial effort; here, savings built up through work.
meaning_usage_profile.connotation: Positive toward the effort and value of the savings, often suggesting that they should not be wasted.
meaning_usage_profile.tone: Conflicted and self-questioning here: the speaker contrasts difficulty justifying the purchase with a strong desire for it.
meaning_usage_profile.register: Common in everyday and financial discussion. It highlights effort, not a particular amount of money.

when_to_use: Emphasize the effort involved in gaining money, success, trust or knowledge.
when_not_to_use: Do not use hard-earned merely to mean expensive; a high price does not describe the effort of earning something.

advanced_nuance: Hard-earned often invites respect for the effort behind an achievement. It can make wasting that achievement seem especially regrettable.
Hard-earned does not prove that an achievement was fair or deserved in every respect; it specifically emphasizes effort.

memory_practice.memory_trigger: Picture many days of work behind a small savings jar.
memory_practice.recall_question: Does hard-earned describe the amount obtained or the effort behind obtaining it?
memory_practice.recognition_task: One prize comes after months of practice; another is won by chance. Which is more naturally called hard-earned? Explain the role of effort.
memory_practice.production_task: Write a short message congratulating a fictional friend on a hard-earned achievement. Mention the work that made the description appropriate.

examples.example_1: She did not want to spend her hard-earned savings on something she would rarely use.
examples.example_2: The team celebrated a hard-earned victory after months of practice.

natural_examples.mini_conversation:
A: Why are you checking the reviews so carefully?
B: I’m spending my hard-earned savings, so I want something that will last.
A: Let’s compare the warranty terms too.

meaning_in_context.source_sentence: "  Meaning:  I  can't  jus tify  spending  our  hard-earned  savings  on  this  expensive  toy ,  but  I  really  want  it.
meaning_in_context.contextual_meaning: gained only after considerable effort or work
meaning_in_context.simple_explanation: The speaker emphasizes the work behind the savings and feels torn about spending them on an expensive toy. Hard-earned highlights effort, not how large the savings are.

mistakes_differences.common_mistake: Incorrect: He spent his hardly-earned savings.
mistakes_differences.correction: Say He spent his hard-earned savings. Hard means with effort here; hardly normally means almost not.
mistakes_differences.important_difference: Hard-earned emphasizes the effort needed to obtain something. Valuable emphasizes its worth; something can be valuable without being hard-earned.

semanticReview.finding: Effort distinguished from price, amount and deservedness; hard/hardly error corrected.
